attributes.title: Level 6

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ What symbol should be added between the 2 conditions inside the parentheses of the if condition?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What symbols create the Boolean AND operator?


Solution: 

& should be added to & in the if condition on Line 200, so that a Boolean AND operator && is formed.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code! 


Notice that the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Line 200: the & operator is not allowed for Boolean types.



Fix the bugs in the code so that the ball sprite moves towards the hoop only if the player sprite overlaps with the ball sprite AND the A button is pressed.

subgroups.title: Debugging Boolean AND Operators and Relational Operators
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: & is changed to && in the if condition on Line 200.
validationItems.failureText: Update the Boolean AND operator in the if condition.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ What symbol should be added inside the parentheses of the if condition under // on countdown end?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which operator checks if a value on the left is greater than or equal to the value on the right?


Solution: 

> is added to = to create a relational operator  >= in the if condition on Line 215.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, a dialog box appears regardless of the user’s score. 


Fix the bugs in the code so that a dialog box only appears if the user scores 6 or more points.

subgroups.title: Debugging Boolean AND Operators and Relational Operators
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: = is changed to the >= relational operator in the if condition on Line 215.
validationItems.failureText: Check the operator used in the if condition under // on countdown end.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Which operation should be used to find how many more baskets the user needed to score?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What variable’s value should be subtracted from 6 to concatenate the number of additional baskets the user needed to score?


Solution: 

- throwsMade should be added inside the parentheses on Line 220, so the code reads:

(6 - throwsMade)
steps.instructions:
When the user doesn’t make 6 baskets by the end of the countdown, a dialog box appears telling the user they needed to make 6 more baskets to win.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the dialog box tells the user exactly how many more baskets they needed to score.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 6 of Blue Belt! Before you create your final Blue Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! In this level, you’ll learn more about Boolean and relational operators, which can be used to check if 1 or more conditions are true in a project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 6:

badges.title: Making Big Decisions
badges.description: Use Boolean and relational operators as part of conditional statements in JavaScript.

badges.title: Package Deal
badges.description: Use a Boolean AND operator in JavaScript.

badges.title: Hard Pressed
badges.description: Check if a button is pressed as part of a conditional statement.

badges.title: Comparatively Speaking
badges.description: Use a relational operator in JavaScript.

badges.title: Reassess the Situation
badges.description: Use an assignment operator to give an existing variable a new value.

badges.title: This or That
badges.description: Use a Boolean OR operator in JavaScript.
